my tears become
a flaw in the design,
my breaking,
you could never hold.

so
when i cry,
when i sorrow,
when i grieve,
when i pain,
when i hurt so wide
i cannot hold myself,

when i shatter 
like glass,
cutting my own 
palms
as i try to gather me—

who will love
me?

for it cannot be you.

the sunlight on my
skin,
reject the storm
in my chest.

yet i’m both.

i see—
how you love me

at the curve
of my mouth,
in the way i smile.
you cup parts of me

like warm tea—
unburdened.

when my voice
trembles,
when grief sits
in my throat,
when sorrow spills

past my lips
